summary: The B05 is Leapmotor's first hatchback in Australia, a rear-drive electric five-door sold from $35,888 list in Style and Design LR grades and aimed squarely at the MG4, BYD Dolphin and GAC Aion UT. Australian launch drives agree the Europe-tuned chassis is the highlight, with CarExpert calling it Leapmotor's most charming vehicle yet and CarsGuide rating it among the best-riding Chinese cars it has driven, but both found the lane-keep and driver-attention systems overbearing and the software in need of polish. It is too new to have Australian long-term or resale history, and Leapmotor has so far sold it mostly on a $35,990 drive-away campaign for the Lightning Yellow Style.
pros: Strong value for a rear-drive 160kW hatch: $35,888 list for the Style with a 56.2kWh LFP pack, 401km WLTP and 0-100km/h in 7.5 seconds, and a $35,990 drive-away offer on Lightning Yellow cars to 31 December 2026

The $39,888 Design LR adds a 67.1kWh pack for 482km WLTP and 174kW DC charging (Style 156kW), plus TechnoLeather, heated front seats and steering wheel, a panoramic roof and a 12-speaker system, and cuts 0-100km/h to 6.7 seconds
Chassis retuned in Europe draws the praise: CarExpert found it balanced and composed on winding roads, and CarsGuide called it one of the best-riding cars it has driven from China
Efficient on test: CarExpert saw 14.6kWh/100km on mostly high-speed rural roads against a 15.8-15.9kWh/100km WLTP claim, with 30-80% DC charging in about 16-18 minutes
Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, a 14.6-inch screen and 360-degree cameras are standard, with eight years of roadside assistance and capped-price servicing and a five-star ANCAP rating
cons: Lane-keep assist is too sensitive and cannot be fully switched off because it is tied to the driver attention monitor, according to CarExpert; CarsGuide also found the driver aids constantly beeping and tugging at the wheel
Not rated to tow in the official specifications: Leapmotor Australia's buyer's guide gives no towing figure and UK reviewers report the B05 cannot tow, even though one Australian database lists 750kg
Boot is small for the class at 357 litres seats up and 1,205 litres folded, with no frunk and no rear wiper
Six-year/150,000km warranty trails the seven years from MG, Kia and GWM, and Leapmotor's thin dealer network and short local history make resale the open risk
Software is unfinished: CarExpert reported a false seatbelt warning and touchscreen lag, and CarsGuide noted screens taking about five seconds to wake, which delays the reversing camera
